name: World War II
blurb: Sling GIs and gliders, fire bazookas, drive Shermans and Rhino tanks, drop paratroopers and call in bombers and battleships.

rifleman.name: Rifleman
rifleman.hint: Drag back to aim, let go to launch. Tap in the air to shout.

para.name: Paratrooper
para.hint: Launch, then tap in the air to pop the parachute. He lands on whoever is below.

engineer.name: Engineer
engineer.hint: Launch, then tap to set off his charge. It goes off by itself after he lands.

sarge.name: Big Sarge
sarge.hint: He's heavy, so pull back hard. Tap in the air to ground-pound straight down.

grenade.name: Grenade
grenade.hint: Drag back to throw. It bounces, then blows up after 3 seconds.

bazooka.name: Bazooka
bazooka.hint: Rockets fly almost straight. Watch the wind!

mortar.name: Mortar
mortar.hint: Aim high so the shell drops down behind walls.

howitzer.name: Howitzer
howitzer.hint: One huge shell with a big blast. Aim carefully.

jeep.name: Jeep
jeep.hint: Tap to roll out. Tap again to jump.

halftrack.name: Halftrack
halftrack.hint: Tap to drive it up to the fort, then tap again and three riflemen jump out.

sherman.name: Sherman
sherman.hint: Tap to roll out. Tap again to fire the main gun (3 shells).

rhino.name: Rhino tank
rhino.hint: A Sherman with steel teeth welded on the front. Tap to roll out, then tap again to ram straight through hedgerows.

bayonet.name: Bayonet charge
bayonet.hint: Launch, then tap to charge forward with the bayonet. He can run right through one soldier and keep going.

glider.name: Glider
glider.hint: A glider has no engine, so launch it hard. Tap in the air and two glider troopers jump out beside it.

p51.name: Mustang
p51.hint: Tap the spot where the Mustang should drop its bombs.

b17.name: Flying Fortress
b17.hint: Tap the middle of the fort. Six bombs fall in a line.

p51s.name: Strafing run
p51s.hint: A Mustang swoops in low with its machine guns blazing. Fighters fly too low and fast for the big flak guns.

p47.name: P-47 Thunderbolt
p47.hint: A tough fighter-bomber. It dives under the flak and drops two bombs right on target.

rockets.name: Rocket attack
rockets.hint: A Thunderbolt fires four rockets that streak down at the target.

b26.name: B-26 Marauder
b26.hint: A medium bomber with four big bombs. It flies high, so the flak guns can shoot it down.

c47.name: C-47 drop
c47.hint: Tap where the paratroopers should jump. Three of them float down onto the fort.

naval.name: Naval guns
naval.hint: Battleships far out at sea fire four giant shells. Tap the target.

campaign.name: Road to the Rhine
campaign.blurb: Lead the U.S. Army from the first paratroopers over Normandy all the way across the Rhine. Every victory earns a reward that makes your army stronger, and every battle is tougher than the last.
campaign.finale: You fought all the way from the night drop over Normandy, across France and Belgium and over the Rhine, and about six weeks after Operation Varsity the war in Europe was won!

rewards.name: Airborne
rewards.text: +1 C-47 paratrooper drop in every battle

rewards.name: Thicker armor
rewards.text: Your jeeps, halftracks and tanks are 40% tougher

rewards.name: Ranger training
rewards.text: Big Sarge and bayonet chargers hit 30% harder

rewards.name: Pole charges
rewards.text: Engineers hit 30% harder when they land

rewards.name: Armored infantry
rewards.text: Halftracks are 40% tougher and crash 30% harder

rewards.name: Gun crews
rewards.text: Mortar and Howitzer shells hit 30% harder on a direct hit

rewards.name: Tank aces
rewards.text: Shermans and Rhino tanks crash and ram 30% harder

rewards.name: Tank hunters
rewards.text: Bazooka rockets hit 30% harder on a direct hit

levels.name: Sainte-Mère-Église
levels.history: On the night before D-Day, thousands of paratroopers of the 82nd Airborne Division jumped into the dark over Normandy. One of them, Private John Steele, got his parachute caught on the church steeple of Sainte-Mère-Église and hung there! By morning the paratroopers had taken the town, one of the very first in France to be freed.
levels.tip: Pop a paratrooper's chute right above a German soldier and he lands on top of him. Grenades bounce, so roll them into the houses.

levels.name: Utah Beach
levels.history: At dawn on D-Day, soldiers of the 4th Infantry Division landed on Utah Beach. Strong currents pushed their boats more than a mile south of the planned spot, so Brigadier General Theodore Roosevelt Jr. looked around and said: “We'll start the war from right here!” Fewer German guns guarded that stretch of sand, and Utah became the easiest of the D-Day beaches.
levels.tip: The Sherman's gun cracks concrete. Lob a mortar shell over the sandbags onto the MG 42 nest.

levels.name: Omaha Beach
levels.history: On D-Day, American soldiers landed on Omaha Beach in Normandy, France. They had to get past steel obstacles, barbed wire and German bunkers on the bluffs above the sand.
levels.tip: Mortar shells drop straight down behind sandbags. Try one on the MG 42 nest.

levels.name: Pointe du Hoc
levels.history: On D-Day, U.S. Army Rangers climbed 100-foot cliffs at Pointe du Hoc with ropes and ladders while German soldiers fired down at them.
levels.tip: The Flak 88 shoots down planes. Knock it out before you call in the Mustang.

levels.name: Brécourt Manor
levels.history: On D-Day morning, Lieutenant Dick Winters and about a dozen paratroopers of Easy Company attacked four big German guns hidden along a hedgerow at Brécourt Manor. The guns were firing at the troops landing on Utah Beach, and the small team knocked out every one of them.
levels.tip: The big guns fire at vehicles, so don't send the halftrack first. Engineers' charges and paratroopers are perfect for wrecking guns.

levels.name: La Fière Causeway
levels.history: Paratroopers of the 82nd Airborne fought to hold the stone bridge at La Fière and the long causeway across the flooded Merderet River. When German tanks (small French-made ones the Germans had captured) rolled toward the bridge, a bazooka team with Private Marcus Heim knocked out the leading tanks. After three days, the airborne soldiers charged across the causeway and opened the road west.
levels.tip: Bazookas are best against tanks, and the tanks fire at anything with wheels. Knock a tank off the bridge and it splashes into the river!

levels.name: Carentan
levels.history: To join up the troops from Utah and Omaha beaches, the 101st Airborne had to capture the town of Carentan, at the end of a long causeway across flooded fields. Lieutenant Colonel Robert Cole led his paratroopers in a bayonet charge on a farm full of German soldiers beside the causeway, and he was awarded the Medal of Honor. The next day, Carentan was free.
levels.tip: Tap the Bayonet charge in mid-air to rush forward and run right through a soldier. The MG 42s knock troops out of the air as they fly past, so take those out first.

levels.name: Fort du Roule
levels.history: To capture the port of Cherbourg, American soldiers had to take Fort du Roule, a German fort dug into a rocky hill high above the harbor. Battleships out at sea fired on the city's guns, and Corporal John Kelly crawled up the hill to blow open a bunker with pole charges.
levels.tip: The Flak 88 shoots down planes, but it can't stop the naval guns. Save the engineers for the concrete bunkers.

levels.name: Saint-Lô
levels.history: For weeks, American soldiers fought through Normandy's hedgerows, tall walls of earth and bushes around every little field, to reach Saint-Lô, the town where the main roads met. When the 29th Infantry Division finally took it on July 18, so much of it had been knocked down that it was later called “the capital of the ruins.”
levels.tip: The MG 42 nests hide behind hedgerows and rubble. Lob mortar shells over them, and save the engineers for the stone walls.

levels.name: Operation Cobra
levels.history: After weeks stuck in the hedgerows, the Americans launched Operation Cobra. Hundreds of bombers pounded a short stretch of the German line, then tanks and troops broke through and raced south. Many Shermans had steel teeth welded on the front, an idea credited to Sergeant Curtis Culin and made from the Germans' own beach obstacles, so these “Rhino” tanks could cut right through the hedgerows.
levels.tip: The 105 mm guns fire at tanks, and the Flak 88s shoot down the Flying Fortress. Send the low-flying Thunderbolt at the flak first, then let the Rhinos ram through the hedgerows.

levels.name: Operation Crossbow
levels.history: Germany hid launch ramps for V-1 “buzz bombs” in the woods of northern France and aimed them at London. The U.S. Army Air Forces and Britain's Royal Air Force hunted the ramps down from the sky in a campaign called Operation Crossbow. Fighter-bombers swooped in low and fast to dodge the big flak guns.
levels.tip: An Air Force mission: everything you have can fly! Fighters sneak under the flak, so use them to knock out the Flak 88s, then send in the bombers.

levels.name: Liberation of Paris
levels.history: In August 1944, the people of Paris rose up against the German soldiers holding their city. The French 2nd Armored Division under General Leclerc rolled in first, with the U.S. 4th Infantry Division right behind, and on August 25 the German commander surrendered. Paris was saved instead of destroyed, and huge crowds cheered in the streets.
levels.tip: The Panzerfaust soldier behind the barricade fires at vehicles. Take him out before you send the Shermans down the street.

levels.name: Siegfried Line
levels.history: By September 1944, the Americans had reached the Siegfried Line on Germany's border: rows of concrete “dragon's teeth” to stop tanks, with pillboxes hidden behind them. On September 11, a small patrol became the first American soldiers to cross into Germany.
levels.tip: Tanks can't get past the dragon's teeth. Blow a gap with the engineers, or fly your troops right over them.

levels.name: Aachen
levels.history: Aachen was the first German city captured by the Allies. Soldiers of the 1st Infantry Division fought through it one building at a time, and they even rolled a huge 155 mm gun up the streets to blast holes in the thick walls. The city surrendered on October 21, 1944.
levels.tip: Panzerfaust soldiers fire at vehicles, so clear the street first. The Howitzer is great for blasting the tall buildings.

levels.name: Hürtgen Forest
levels.history: The Hürtgen Forest was a dark, thick pine forest on Germany's border, full of hidden log bunkers. In the cold autumn rain and deep mud, tanks could barely move, and American soldiers fought there for months in one of the hardest battles of the war.
levels.tip: Snipers and MG 42s hide in log bunkers among the trees. Mortars drop right onto the bunker roofs, and the muddy ditches can trap your tank.

levels.name: Bastogne
levels.history: In the snowy winter of 1944, American paratroopers were surrounded at Bastogne, Belgium. When the Germans told them to surrender, General McAuliffe answered with one word: “Nuts!” Patton's tanks broke through the day after Christmas.
levels.tip: The Tiger fires at your vehicles. Hit it with the Bazooka before you send the Sherman.

levels.name: Remagen Bridge
levels.history: American soldiers reached the Ludendorff Bridge over the Rhine River and were amazed to find it still standing. The Germans set off their explosives, but the bridge stayed up! Sergeant Alexander Drabik was the first to run across, and it became the first bridge over the Rhine that the Allies captured.
levels.tip: Drive across the bridge, but don't fall in the river. The Flak 88 on the cliff shoots down planes, so knock it out before you call the Mustang.

levels.name: Operation Varsity
levels.history: In Operation Varsity, thousands of planes and gliders carried American and British airborne soldiers across the Rhine River in a single morning. They landed right on top of the German positions near the town of Wesel, the biggest airborne drop ever made in one day, and soon joined up with the troops crossing the river in boats.
levels.tip: Snipers shoot down parachutes and flak guns shoot down high-flying planes. Knock them out with gliders and the low-flying Thunderbolt before the big drops.
